need: The `/var/log/` folder of a Linux machine, or a triage or image that contains it
masstin installed
Knowing what an SSH session is
steps: Find out the distribution: on Red Hat and similar look at `/var/log/secure`; on Debian and Ubuntu, `/var/log/auth.log`.
Search for `Accepted` lines (successful login) and `Failed password` lines (failure). Note the user, source IP and time.
Review `/var/log/audit/audit.log` and look at the `USER_LOGIN` and `USER_AUTH` records.
Read the binary files with `last -f /var/log/wtmp`, `lastb -f /var/log/btmp` and `lastlog`.
If `auth.log` is almost empty, the SSH activity is in the journal, under `/var/log/journal/<machine-id>/`.

Read in the output what masstin inferred: hostname, year and time zone.
terms: SSH
A protocol to open a remote session on another machine; on Linux almost all remote access goes through it.
auth.log / secure
The text file where Linux writes authentication attempts; the name depends on the distribution.
auditd
The Linux audit subsystem, which writes detailed records to `/var/log/audit/audit.log`.
wtmp / btmp
Binary files with the session history (wtmp) and the failed attempts (btmp).
systemd-journald
A service that stores logs in binary `.journal` files instead of text.
Password spraying
Trying a few passwords against many different users.

The Active Directory authentication system, based on tickets issued by the domain controller.

A Windows authentication protocol older than Kerberos.
Log rotation
When the file fills up, new events overwrite the oldest ones.

The Windows protocol to share files and printers over the network.
Share
A folder or resource shared over the network, such as `ADMIN$` or `C$`.
PsExec

Null session
An anonymous connection, with no user or password.
Share enumeration
Going through the shared resources of the network to see which ones are reachable.

Shell

need: Proxmox VE installed and the ISOs downloaded (Part 1)
Root SSH access to the host and to the Proxmox VNC console
Comfort with the Linux terminal
steps: Create each Windows machine with `qm create`, with three CD-ROMs (the Windows ISO, `virtio-win.iso` and the autounattend ISO) and the network on `tag=10`.
Find the edition index with `wiminfo /mnt/iso/sources/install.wim` and put it in `/IMAGE/INDEX` inside `autounattend.xml`.
Pack the file into a small ISO with `genisoimage -o autounattend-2019.iso -J -r ${TMPDIR}/` and attach it as `ide3`.
For Ubuntu, import the cloud image with `qm importdisk 107 jammy-server-cloudimg-amd64.img local-zfs`, configure cloud-init with `qm set 107` and then install `qemu-guest-agent` over SSH.
For Kali, inject `preseed.cfg` into the initrd, repack the ISO and, after installing, run `qm set 108 --delete ide2` and `qm set 108 --boot order=scsi0`.
On each Windows machine, open the VNC console, run `D:\virtio-win-guest-tools.exe` and reboot with `Restart-Computer -Force`.
Give each machine its IP and name with `qm guest exec`, remove the install ISOs and set `--boot order=scsi0`.

cloud-init
A mechanism that sets up user, network and SSH on the first boot of a ready-made Linux image.
Preseed
A file holding the answers for the Debian or Kali installer so that it asks nothing.
initrd
The small boot system that loads the installer before any disk exists.

learn: Install pfSense by hand over VNC and assign its WAN and LAN interfaces
Understand how pfSense separates the corporate network (VLAN 10) from the attack network (VLAN 20) and does NAT
Check that Kali goes out through pfSense and that NAT is active

need: The virtual machines from Part 2 and the pfSense ISO
Access to the Proxmox VNC console and SSH to the host
The WireGuard client on your PC
steps: Boot VM 100 from the pfSense ISO and install: Accept, Install, **Auto (ZFS)**, Stripe and tick the `da0` disk.
Before the first boot remove the ISO: `qm stop 100 --timeout 5`, `qm set 100 --delete ide2`, `qm set 100 --boot order=scsi0` and `qm start 100`.
In the first questions answer **n** to VLANs, `vtnet0` for WAN and `vtnet1` for LAN.
With option **2** set the WAN to `192.168.10.2` with gateway `192.168.10.1`, and the LAN to `192.168.20.1` with DHCP from `192.168.20.50` to `192.168.20.99`. Enable SSH with option **14**.
On the host, free the old IP with `ip addr del 192.168.20.1/24 dev vmbr0.20` and add the management one with `ip addr add 192.168.20.254/24 dev vmbr0.20`.
Check Kali with `qm guest exec 108 -- bash -c "ip route show; ping -c 2 192.168.20.1"` and NAT on pfSense with `pfctl -sn | grep -i nat`.
Create `/etc/wireguard/wg0.conf` on the host, start it with `systemctl enable --now wg-quick@wg0`, configure the client on your PC and test with `ping 192.168.10.10`.
terms: pfSense
A router and firewall system that here decides which traffic passes between the lab's two networks.
VLAN
An isolated virtual network inside the same physical network.
NAT
Address translation: traffic leaves with the firewall's IP instead of the machine's real IP.
Pivoting
Going through an intermediate machine to reach another network.
WireGuard
A small, fast VPN that builds an encrypted tunnel between two machines that exchange public keys.
Gateway
The address a machine sends all traffic to when it is bound for outside its own network.

learn: Install Sysmon with the sysmon-modular configuration on the Windows machines through Ansible

need: The deployed domain and the Ansible inventory (Part 4)
Root access to the Proxmox host
Basic knowledge of Windows event logs
steps: Download Sysmon and the configuration on the host: `wget https://download.sysinternals.com/files/Sysmon.zip` and `wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/olafhartong/sysmon-modular/master/sysmonconfig.xml`.
Apply the playbook, which copies the files to `C:\sysmon` and installs with `C:\sysmon\Sysmon64.exe -accepteula -i C:\sysmon\sysmonconfig.xml`.
Enable the audit subcategories, for example `auditpol /set /subcategory:"Kerberos Service Ticket Operations" /success:enable /failure:enable`.
Enable the command line in 4688 with the `ProcessCreationIncludeCmdLine_Enabled` value, and PowerShell logging with `EnableScriptBlockLogging`, `EnableModuleLogging` and `EnableTranscripting`.
Cap the log sizes, for example with `wevtutil sl Security /ms:536870912`.
On Ubuntu, load the auditd rules and try a search with `sudo ausearch -k sudo_exec --start recent`.
Verify: `(Get-Service sysmon64).Status` must return Running and `sudo auditctl -l | wc -l` must return 50.
terms: Sysmon
A Windows tool that records processes, network connections, files and registry changes in detail.
EVTX
The file format in which Windows stores its event logs.
Audit subcategory
Each fine-grained group of Windows security events, which must be enabled with `auditpol` to be recorded.
Script Block Logging
The record (event 4104) of every block of code PowerShell runs.
auditd
The Linux service that records executions, file access and other actions according to a set of rules.
DCSync
The attack in which someone poses as a domain controller to pull password hashes through replication.

allymacb installed

steps: Run `allymacb -f disk.E01 -o timeline.csv`.
Look at the `[ALERT]` lines at the end of the run: they are the files the rules give as `significant`.

Filter the timeline on that same time and look at what else was created around it.

terms: MACB
The four dates of a file: modification, access, metadata change and birth (creation).
`$MFT`
The NTFS table that keeps one record per file, with its name and its dates.
USN journal

timestomping
Changing the dates of a file by hand so that it looks older.

Changing the dates of a file by hand so that it looks older.

Each of the files in which Windows stores the registry.
process tree
The relation of which process started which, from parent to child.
USN journal
An NTFS record that notes every change made to the files of a volume.

Reconstruir una historia juntando varias fuentes que apuntan al mismo segundo.

Distinguir los hallazgos del hunt del ruido conocido antes de fiarte de las cifras.

caarea instalado
Un visor de CSV

Mira el resumen de la consola: lo `significant` sale arriba, agrupado por fichero, con las reglas que saltaron.
Abre el CSV, ve a la hora de un hallazgo y lee las filas de alrededor. Cada fuente cuenta una parte de lo mismo.
Mira la línea `lineage:` de una fila juzgada para ver de qué proceso cuelga el binario.
Mira la columna `state` para saber cómo se obtuvo cada fila: `live`, `vss`, `deleted`, `txlog` o `carved`.

Ficheros que Windows crea al ejecutar un programa y que dejan constancia de que se ejecutó.

hive

learn: Tell apart the two levels of recovery: what the file system still describes and what only remains as loose bytes.

Decide when `--carve` is worth using and what it will not recover.
need: A full disk image (carving reads the whole disk)
One of the tools installed: masstin, faramir, allymacb or caarea
Knowing what the `$MFT` and a registry hive are
steps: Run the tool normally. Level one is always read: look at the rows with state `deleted`, `vss` or `removed_since_vss`.
Decide whether you need more: the logs were cleared, the volume was formatted or reinstalled, or you need to know what was there before.
If so, repeat the run adding `--carve`. Expect it to read the whole disk and take much longer.
Look at the `Carving:` summary on the console to see how much of what was found was not already in the live table.
In the timeline, filter on `carved`. Each row carries the exact position, for example `(carved @0x2D20990A8)`, so it can be checked.
Discard the obvious rubbish: in the example, `utmp` records dated 1995 on a Windows volume.
Remember the limits: what is recovered is the trace of the file, not its content, and on an SSD with TRIM there may be nothing left.
terms: carving
Walking the bytes of a disk looking for structures by their shape, when nothing says where they are any more.
free space
The area of the disk that the file system considers empty, but which can still hold old bytes.
shadow copy
A snapshot of a Windows volume as it was at an earlier moment.
The index of an NTFS folder, which keeps file names even after the files were deleted.
TRIM
A feature of SSD disks that really erases the blocks that were freed.
`[ORPHAN]`
The mark of a recovered file whose parent folder could not be recovered.

learn: Distinguir los dos niveles de recuperación: lo que el sistema de ficheros todavía describe y lo que solo queda en bytes sueltos.
Saber qué busca `--carve` en cada herramienta y cuánto cuesta.
Reconocer una fila recuperada por carving y la posición en la que se encontró.
Decidir cuándo merece la pena usar `--carve` y qué no va a recuperar.
need: Una imagen de disco completa (el carving lee el disco entero)
Alguna de las herramientas instalada: masstin, faramir, allymacb o caarea
Saber qué son el `$MFT` y un hive del registro
steps: Ejecuta la herramienta de forma normal. El nivel uno se lee siempre: mira las filas con estado `deleted`, `vss` o `removed_since_vss`.
Decide si necesitas más: se vaciaron los logs, el volumen se formateó o reinstaló, o hay que saber qué había antes.
Si es así, repite la ejecución añadiendo `--carve`. Cuenta con que lee el disco entero y tarda mucho más.
Mira el resumen `Carving:` de la consola para ver cuánto de lo encontrado no estaba ya en la tabla viva.
En la timeline, filtra por `carved`. Cada fila lleva la posición exacta, por ejemplo `(carved @0x2D20990A8)`, para poder comprobarla.
Descarta la basura evidente: en el ejemplo, registros `utmp` con fechas de 1995 en un volumen de Windows.
Recuerda los límites: se recupera el rastro del fichero, no su contenido, y en un SSD con TRIM puede no quedar nada.
terms: carving
Recorrer los bytes de un disco buscando estructuras por su forma, cuando ya no hay nada que diga dónde están.
espacio libre
Zona del disco que el sistema de ficheros da por vacía, pero que aún puede guardar bytes antiguos.
copia de sombra
Instantánea de un volumen de Windows tal como estaba en un momento anterior.
Índice de una carpeta de NTFS, que conserva nombres de ficheros aunque ya se hayan borrado.
TRIM
Función de los discos SSD que borra de verdad los bloques liberados.
`[ORPHAN]`
Marca de un fichero recuperado cuya carpeta padre ya no se pudo recuperar.

learn: Understand what each of the three libraries does: evidencefs, blockcarve and dirtyhive.
Know how evidencefs turns any evidence into a list of read-only mounts.
Understand why a hive copied from a running machine is incomplete without its transaction logs.
Know which tools already use each library and which do not yet.
need: Knowing the tools of the family as a user
Some Rust, if you want to use the libraries in your own code
steps: First read which library is under which tool: blockcarve is already in the four main ones; evidencefs, today, in etcdump.
In evidencefs, open an evidence with `Evidence::open("disk.E01".as_ref(), &OpenOptions::default())?` and look at what `ev.describe()` prints.
Notice the line of the `vss` mount: the shadow copy is read like one more volume. Deleted files appear under `/$DELETED/`.
In blockcarve, go through what each structure has to prove before being accepted: hive, event log chunk and `$MFT` record.
In dirtyhive, open a hive with `Hive::open(path, &opts)?`, look at `hive.info().summary()` and walk `hive.deleted()` to see the deleted keys.
Finish with the section on what they do not do yet, to know the limits before using them.
terms: A common forensic disk image format, often split into several segments.
mount
A read-only file system that evidencefs returns and that is walked the same way wherever it comes from.
shadow copy
A snapshot of a Windows volume as it was at an earlier moment.
carving
Walking the bytes of a disk looking for structures by their shape, when no file points to them any more.
hive
Each of the files in which Windows stores the registry.
transaction logs
The `.LOG1` and `.LOG2` files where Windows notes registry changes before moving them into the hive.

learn: Entender qué hace cada una de las tres bibliotecas: evidencefs, blockcarve y dirtyhive.
Saber cómo evidencefs convierte cualquier evidencia en una lista de montajes de solo lectura.
Entender por qué un hive copiado de una máquina encendida está incompleto sin sus logs de transacciones.
Saber cuáles de las herramientas usan ya cada biblioteca y cuáles todavía no.
need: Conocer las herramientas de la familia a nivel de usuario
Nociones de Rust, si quieres usar las bibliotecas en tu propio código
steps: Lee primero qué biblioteca hay debajo de qué herramienta: blockcarve ya está en las cuatro principales; evidencefs, hoy, en etcdump.
En evidencefs, abre una evidencia con `Evidence::open("disk.E01".as_ref(), &OpenOptions::default())?` y mira lo que imprime `ev.describe()`.
Fíjate en la línea del montaje `vss`: la copia de sombra se lee como un volumen más. Los ficheros borrados aparecen bajo `/$DELETED/`.
En blockcarve, repasa qué tiene que demostrar cada estructura antes de aceptarse: hive, trozo de log de eventos y registro del `$MFT`.
En dirtyhive, abre un hive con `Hive::open(path, &opts)?`, mira `hive.info().summary()` y recorre `hive.deleted()` para ver las claves borradas.
Acaba por «Lo que todavía no hacen» para conocer los límites antes de usarlas.
terms: Formato habitual de imagen forense de disco, a menudo partido en varios segmentos.
montaje
Sistema de ficheros de solo lectura que evidencefs devuelve y que se recorre igual venga de donde venga.
copia de sombra
Instantánea de un volumen de Windows tal como estaba en un momento anterior.
carving
Recorrer los bytes de un disco buscando estructuras por su forma, cuando ya no hay fichero que las señale.
hive
Cada uno de los ficheros en los que Windows guarda el registro.
logs de transacciones
Ficheros `.LOG1` y `.LOG2` donde Windows apunta los cambios del registro antes de pasarlos al hive.

learn: Dump the configuration of a Linux system (accounts, sudo, SSH, cron, systemd...) to readable text per area.
Find with `grep` what the rules marked, by searching for `<<<`.
Tell a `candidate` line from a `habitual` one that ships with the system.
Measure a clean machine of your own to lower the noise.
need: A Linux triage (`.tgz`, zip, tar or a folder with `etc/passwd`) or a disk image
etcdump installed
Basic use of `grep` and `diff`
steps: Run `etcdump -f lnx01-triage.tgz -o lnx01-etc --summary`.
Look at the area table on the console: the `hits` column says where a rule fired.
Open the text file of one area, for example sudo, and look for the `<<<` mark.
Get everything that was marked with `grep -h "<<<" lnx01-etc/*.txt`.
Ask concrete questions with `grep -i nopasswd lnx01-etc/*_sudo.txt`, or compare two servers with `diff a_ssh.txt b_ssh.txt`.
Open `timeline.csv` to see each item at the modification date of its file. That date belongs to the whole file, not to the line.
If there is a lot of factory noise, measure a clean machine: `etcdump -d clean-image --measure -o measured` and then `etcdump -f suspect.tgz --reference measured/reference.tsv -o out`.
terms: triage
A quick collection of the most useful files of a machine, without copying the whole disk.
sudoers
The Linux file that says who can run commands as administrator with `sudo`.
`NOPASSWD`
A sudoers option that allows using `sudo` without typing the password.
cron
The Linux system that runs jobs at fixed times.
`shadow`
The Linux file that stores the encrypted passwords (hashes) of the accounts.
`ld.so.preload`
A Linux file that forces every program to load a given library.

learn: Volcar la configuración de un Linux (cuentas, sudo, SSH, cron, systemd...) a texto legible por área.
Encontrar con `grep` lo que marcaron las reglas, buscando `<<<`.
Distinguir una línea `candidate` de una `habitual` que viene de fábrica.
Medir una máquina limpia propia para bajar el ruido.

etcdump instalado
Saber usar `grep` y `diff` a nivel básico

Mira la tabla de áreas de la consola: la columna `hits` dice dónde saltó alguna regla.
Abre el fichero de texto de un área, por ejemplo el de sudo, y busca la marca `<<<`.
Saca todo lo marcado con `grep -h "<<<" lnx01-etc/*.txt`.

terms: triage
Recogida rápida de los ficheros más útiles de una máquina, sin copiar el disco entero.
sudoers
Fichero de Linux que dice quién puede ejecutar órdenes como administrador con `sudo`.
`NOPASSWD`
Opción de sudoers que permite usar `sudo` sin escribir la contraseña.
cron
Sistema de Linux que ejecuta tareas a horas fijas.
`shadow`
Fichero de Linux que guarda las contraseñas cifradas (hashes) de las cuentas.
`ld.so.preload`
Fichero de Linux que obliga a todos los programas a cargar una biblioteca concreta.

learn: Understand which question each tool answers: logons, execution, persistence and files.
Cross several timelines by filtering all of them on the same time interval.
Recognise what each tool knows and what it cannot know on its own.
Identify the five shared final columns: `hunt`, `hunt_score`, `hunt_why`, `verdict` and `notes`.
need: A case folder with a disk image or triages
masstin, caarea, faramir and allymacb installed
A CSV viewer
steps: Run `masstin -a parse -d case/ -o logins.csv` to get the logons.
Run `caarea -d case/ -o execution.csv --hunt` to get what was executed.
Run `faramir -d case/ -o persistence.csv` and `allymacb -f case/images/dev-srv01.vmdk -o files.csv`.
Look at what each tool puts at the very top. Each finding is a separate lead.
Filter the four timelines on the same time interval and read them together, top to bottom.
For each row, ask which tool gives it and what is missing: who got in, what ran, what will keep running and when each file arrived.
Write your decision in `verdict` and `notes`. No tool writes in those two columns.
terms: timeline
A list of events sorted by time, one row per event.
triage
A quick collection of the most useful files of a machine, without copying the whole disk.
Run key
A Windows registry entry that starts a program every time someone logs on.
scheduled task
An order stored in Windows to run something at a fixed time or frequency.
`$MFT`
The NTFS table that keeps one record per file, with its name and its dates.
UTC
Universal time, with no time zone, which lets you compare events from different machines.

learn: Entender qué pregunta responde cada herramienta: logins, ejecución, persistencia y ficheros.
Cruzar varias timelines filtrándolas todas por el mismo intervalo de hora.
Reconocer qué sabe cada herramienta y qué no puede saber por sí sola.
Identificar las cinco columnas finales comunes: `hunt`, `hunt_score`, `hunt_why`, `verdict` y `notes`.
need: Una carpeta de caso con una imagen de disco o triages
masstin, caarea, faramir y allymacb instalados
Un visor de CSV
steps: Ejecuta `masstin  -a parse -d caso/ -o logins.csv` para sacar los inicios de sesión.
Ejecuta `caarea   -d caso/ -o ejecucion.csv --hunt` para sacar lo que se ejecutó.
Ejecuta `faramir  -d caso/ -o persistencia.csv` y `allymacb -f caso/images/dev-srv01.vmdk -o ficheros.csv`.
Mira qué pone cada herramienta arriba del todo. Cada hallazgo es una pista suelta.
Filtra las cuatro timelines por el mismo intervalo de hora y léelas juntas, de arriba abajo.
Pregúntate en cada fila qué herramienta la da y qué le falta: quién entró, qué se ejecutó, qué va a seguir ejecutándose y cuándo llegó cada fichero.
Apunta tu decisión en `verdict` y `notes`. Ninguna herramienta escribe en esas dos columnas.
terms: timeline
Lista de eventos ordenados por hora, una fila por evento.
triage
Recogida rápida de los ficheros más útiles de una máquina, sin copiar el disco entero.
clave Run
Entrada del registro de Windows que lanza un programa cada vez que alguien inicia sesión.
tarea programada
Orden guardada en Windows para ejecutar algo a una hora o con una frecuencia fija.
`$MFT`
Tabla de NTFS que guarda un registro por cada fichero, con su nombre y sus fechas.
UTC
Hora universal, sin zona horaria, que permite comparar eventos de máquinas distintas.

learn: Interpret the states of the `hunt` column: `significant`, `candidate`, `habitual`, `baseline` and `not_evaluated`.
Read `hunt_score` as rarity from 0 to 100, where every ten points are one order of magnitude.
Understand that the points of a rule are measured on clean machines, not set by whoever wrote it.
Read `hunt_why` and separate what the rules say from what the statistics say.
need: A timeline with hunt from any of the tools
Basic notions of probability (what 'one in a thousand' means)
steps: Open a timeline and find the three final hunt columns: `hunt`, `hunt_score` and `hunt_why`.
Read `hunt`: `significant` passes the bar, `candidate` deserves a look, `habitual` is vouched for by something.
Read `hunt_score` as rarity: 20 is one in a hundred, 30 one in a thousand. Filter on `hunt_score >= 30` to see what is rarer than one in a thousand.
Read `hunt_why`: rules come first, strongest to weakest, then the statistics. Filter on `rule ` to keep only the rules.
Check how much reference there is. With no reference days or rows there are no statistics, and then the rules are the reliable part.
Sort by rarity and decide yourself. The decision goes in `verdict`, where no tool writes.
terms: hunt
An automatic pass that marks the rarest rows of a timeline so you look at them first.
rule
A check with its own identifier that fires when a row has a shape known to be suspicious.
clean reference
Data from machines with no incident, used to compare against what is being investigated.
baseline
What is older than the start date you gave; it is used for comparison and is not judged.
Benjamini-Hochberg
A statistical correction that limits false findings when thousands of rows are looked at together.
timestomping
Changing the dates of a file by hand so that it looks older.

learn: Interpretar los estados de la columna `hunt`: `significant`, `candidate`, `habitual`, `baseline` y `not_evaluated`.
Leer `hunt_score` como rareza de 0 a 100, donde cada diez puntos son un orden de magnitud.
Entender que los puntos de una regla se miden en máquinas limpias y no los pone quien la escribe.
Leer `hunt_why` y separar lo que dicen las reglas de lo que dice la estadística.
need: Una timeline con hunt de cualquiera de las herramientas
Nociones básicas de probabilidad (qué es «una de cada mil»)
steps: Abre una timeline y localiza las tres columnas finales del hunt: `hunt`, `hunt_score` y `hunt_why`.
Lee `hunt`: `significant` pasa el listón, `candidate` merece un vistazo, `habitual` está avalado por algo.
Lee `hunt_score` como rareza: 20 es una de cada cien, 30 una de cada mil. Filtra por `hunt_score >= 30` para ver lo más raro que uno entre mil.
Lee `hunt_why`: primero van las reglas, de la más fuerte a la más débil, y luego la estadística. Filtra por `rule ` para quedarte solo con las reglas.
Comprueba cuánta referencia hay. Sin días o filas de referencia no hay estadística, y entonces las reglas son lo fiable.
Ordena por rareza y decide tú. La decisión va en `verdict`, donde ninguna herramienta escribe.
terms: hunt
Pasada automática que marca las filas más raras de una timeline para que las mires primero.
regla
Comprobación con identificador propio que salta cuando una fila tiene una forma conocida como sospechosa.
referencia limpia
Datos de máquinas sin incidente con los que se compara lo que se investiga.
baseline
Lo anterior a la fecha de inicio que diste; sirve de comparación y no se juzga.
Benjamini-Hochberg
Corrección estadística que limita los falsos hallazgos cuando se miran miles de filas a la vez.
timestomping
Cambiar a mano las fechas de un fichero para que parezca más antiguo.

learn: Get every Windows and Linux persistence mechanism of a case into one timeline.
Read the hunt summary to keep what is significant and candidate instead of thousands of entries.
Understand that each row goes through two engines, rules and statistics, and read the reason in `hunt_why`.
Know where deleted persistence comes from and why dirty hives matter.
need: A disk image, a triage, a mounted volume or a registry hive
faramir installed
A CSV viewer
steps: Run `faramir -d /evidence/case -o persistence.csv`.
Look at the `Hunt:` line on the console. What matters are the first three figures: significant, candidate and habitual.
Open the CSV and leave what is `habitual` for last. Start with `significant` and go on with `candidate`.
Read `hunt_why` on each row to know which rule fired or what the statistics said.
Review the rows with state `deleted` or `removed_since_vss`: something that started by itself and is no longer there.
If there is a lot of noise in your network, use `--known-good` with the CSV of a clean machine or `--baseline` with the date until which the system was trustworthy.
Cross what you find with the file timeline to know when it arrived and what came with it.
terms: persistence
Any mechanism that makes a program run again after a reboot or a logon.
Run key
A Windows registry entry that starts a program every time someone logs on.
dirty hive
A registry file that lacks the latest changes, which are still in its transaction logs.
shadow copy
A snapshot of a Windows volume as it was at an earlier moment.
`authorized_keys`
A Linux file with the SSH keys allowed to enter an account without a password.
ATT&CK
A public catalogue of attack techniques, each with its identifier (for example T1547).

learn: Sacar en una timeline todos los mecanismos de persistencia de Windows y Linux de un caso.
Leer el resumen del hunt para quedarte con lo significativo y lo candidato en vez de con miles de entradas.
Entender que cada fila pasa por dos motores, reglas y estadística, y leer el motivo en `hunt_why`.
Saber de dónde sale la persistencia borrada y por qué importan los hives sucios.

faramir instalado
Un visor de CSV

Mira la línea `Hunt:` de la consola. Lo que importa son las tres primeras cifras: significant, candidate y habitual.
Abre el CSV y deja lo `habitual` para el final. Empieza por lo `significant` y sigue por lo `candidate`.
Lee `hunt_why` en cada fila para saber qué regla saltó o qué dijo la estadística.
Revisa las filas con estado `deleted` o `removed_since_vss`: algo que arrancaba solo y ya no está.
Si hay mucho ruido en tu red, usa `--known-good` con el CSV de una máquina limpia o `--baseline` con la fecha hasta la que el sistema era de fiar.
Cruza lo que encuentres con la timeline de ficheros para saber cuándo llegó y qué vino con él.
terms: persistencia
Cualquier mecanismo que hace que un programa vuelva a ejecutarse tras reiniciar o iniciar sesión.
clave Run
Entrada del registro de Windows que lanza un programa cada vez que alguien inicia sesión.
hive sucio
Fichero del registro al que le faltan los últimos cambios, que siguen en sus logs de transacciones.
copia de sombra
Instantánea de un volumen de Windows tal como estaba en un momento anterior.
`authorized_keys`
Fichero de Linux con las claves SSH que pueden entrar en una cuenta sin contraseña.
ATT&CK
Catálogo público de técnicas de ataque, cada una con su identificador (por ejemplo T1547).

Basic notions of the Windows registry and of Linux configuration

terms: service
A Windows program that starts by itself with the system and runs in the background.
DLL
A code library that a Windows program loads in order to work.
COM hijacking
Changing in the registry which DLL is loaded when a program asks for a Windows component.
Winlogon
The Windows process that handles logon and loads several programs while doing so.
systemd
The Linux system that starts services and scheduled jobs (timers).
`ld.so.preload`
A Linux file that forces every program to load a given library.

Nociones básicas del registro de Windows y de la configuración de Linux
faramir instalado, si quieres probar los comandos

Mira la tabla de reparto para situarte: casi todo son servicios, y las claves Run son muy pocas.

learn: Understand how masstin reads VPN, firewall or proxy logs with YAML rule files

regex
Regular expression: a pattern used to find and extract pieces of text from a line.

A log shape where each piece of data is a key and a value, such as `user=ana`.

A file with one JSON object per line.

The list of lines that no rule was able to read.

An attacker moving from one machine to another inside the network.

Expresión regular: un patrón para buscar y extraer trozos de texto de una línea.

terms: Carving
Recovering data by searching for its signatures directly in the disk bytes, without using the file system.
Unallocated space
Areas of the disk marked as free that may still hold data from deleted files.
Chunk
A 64 KB block of an EVTX file, which can be read on its own.
Record
Each individual event stored inside a chunk.
Signature (magic)
A fixed sequence of bytes that a kind of data starts with, such as `ElfChnk`.
BinXML
The compact binary encoding in which EVTX stores the content of each event.

Recuperar datos buscando sus firmas directamente en los bytes del disco, sin usar el sistema de ficheros.
Espacio no asignado
Zonas del disco marcadas como libres que aún pueden contener datos de ficheros borrados.
Chunk
Bloque de 64 KB de un fichero EVTX, que se puede leer por sí solo.
Record
Cada evento individual guardado dentro de un chunk.
Firma (magic)
Secuencia fija de bytes con la que empieza un tipo de dato, como `ElfChnk`.
BinXML
Codificación binaria compacta en la que EVTX guarda el contenido de cada evento.

terms: lateral movement
An attacker moving from one machine to another inside the network.
baseline
The days before the incident, which the hunt uses to learn what is normal in that network.
p-value
A number that says how likely it is to see something this rare on a normal day; the lower, the rarer.
false discovery rate (FDR)
The share of false findings you accept; it is the only number you choose.
seed
A machine, address or account you already know is compromised, from which the chain is rebuilt.
credential switch
An account used from a machine that had never used it.

terms: movimiento lateral
Paso de un atacante de una máquina a otra dentro de la red.
línea base
Los días anteriores al incidente, que el hunt usa para aprender qué es normal en esa red.
p-valor
Número que dice cómo de probable es ver algo así de raro en un día normal; cuanto más bajo, más raro.
tasa de falsos descubrimientos (FDR)
La proporción de hallazgos falsos que aceptas; es el único número que eliges.
semilla
Una máquina, dirección o cuenta que ya sabes que está comprometida y desde la que se reconstruye la cadena.

terms: reference (baseline)
The period before what you investigate, used to know what is normal.
habitual connection
A connection that had already happened in the reference; it is not examined.
significant
The status of a connection that is new and too rare to be chance.
credential switch
An account that belongs to other machines, used from one that had never used it.
brute force
Trying many passwords in a row until one works.
jump server
An intermediate machine administrators go through to reach others.

terms: referencia (baseline)
El periodo anterior a lo que investigas, que sirve para saber qué es normal.
conexión habitual
Una conexión que ya había ocurrido en la referencia; no se examina.
significant
Estado de una conexión nueva y demasiado rara para ser casualidad.
cambio de credencial
Una cuenta que es de otras máquinas, usada desde una que nunca la había usado.
fuerza bruta
Probar muchas contraseñas seguidas hasta acertar.
servidor de salto
Máquina intermedia por la que los administradores entran a otras.

Everything before the date you choose; the hunt uses it to know what is normal.

Paso de un atacante de una máquina a otra dentro de la red.

Todo lo anterior a la fecha que eliges; el hunt lo usa para saber qué es normal.

Probar muchas contraseñas seguidas hasta acertar.

Cuenta que usa un programa, no una persona; aquí, la de SQL.
controlador de dominio
Servidor que guarda las cuentas del dominio y valida los inicios de sesión.

steps: Connect the disk through a write blocker and note the drive letter it gets, or log on to the running system.

A full copy of a disk in a file; making one can take hours.
raw volume
The disk content read directly, without going through the Windows file system.

Collecting the essentials of a machine while it is running.

A trace Windows leaves when a program runs.

Copia completa de un disco en un fichero; hacerla puede llevar horas.
volumen en bruto
El contenido del disco leído directamente, sin pasar por el sistema de ficheros de Windows.
bloqueador de escritura
Aparato que deja leer un disco pero impide escribir en él.
copias de sombra (VSS)
Instantáneas antiguas del volumen que Windows guarda y que pueden conservar logs ya borrados.

Recoger lo esencial de una máquina mientras está encendida.
prefetch
Rastro que Windows deja cuando se ejecuta un programa.

learn: Pick the masstin binary that matches your Mac: Apple Silicon or Intel

need: A Mac with macOS 11 or later and access to the Terminal
Knowing whether your Mac is Apple Silicon (M1 to M4) or Intel
A folder with logs for the test
steps: Check which processor your Mac has and pick `masstin-macos-arm64` (Apple Silicon) or `masstin-macos-x86_64` (Intel).
Download the binary: `curl -LO https://github.com/jupyterj0nes/masstin/releases/latest/download/masstin-<tag>-macos-arm64`.

Parse a folder of logs: `./masstin-<tag>-macos-arm64 -a parse -d /evidence/logs -o timeline.csv`.
terms: Apple Silicon / arm64
Apple's own processors (M1, M2, M3, M4) and the name of their architecture.
Rosetta 2
The macOS layer that translates Intel programs so they run on Apple Silicon, somewhat slower.
Gatekeeper
The macOS protection that blocks the first run of unsigned downloaded programs.
quarantine
A mark (`com.apple.quarantine`) macOS puts on some downloaded files.
binary
The program's executable file, already compiled.
A common forensic disk image format.

learn: Elegir el binario de masstin que corresponde a tu Mac: Apple Silicon o Intel

Los procesadores de Apple (M1, M2, M3, M4) y el nombre de su arquitectura.

Capa de macOS que traduce programas de Intel para que corran en Apple Silicon, algo más despacio.

Protección de macOS que bloquea la primera ejecución de programas descargados sin firmar.

Marca (`com.apple.quarantine`) que macOS pone a algunos ficheros descargados.

A database that stores nodes and the relationships between them, instead of tables.

A program that runs applications inside ready-made containers.

The Windows subsystem that runs Linux, required by Docker Desktop.

A chain of hops between machines where each hop happens after the previous one.

Lenguaje de consultas para grafos que usan Memgraph y Neo4j.

learn: Join several timelines into one, sorted and without duplicates
Keep your verdicts and notes when you parse again, with `--carry-marks`
Read the final `merge` summary and know what each counter means
Re-filter or cut down in time a timeline you already have
need: masstin installed
Two or more masstin CSV timelines (or just one, if you are filtering it or carrying marks into it)
steps: Gather the timelines of each delivery of the case.
Join them: `masstin -a merge -f monday.csv -f wednesday.csv -f vpn.csv -o case.csv`.
Read the `Merge: ... rows written` line and check that `malformed` is 0.
If you parsed again and had marks, bring them over: `masstin -a merge -f new1.csv -f new2.csv -o case-v2.csv --carry-marks case-v1.csv`.
Look at how many rows took their mark and compare it with the marked rows in the earlier one: the two should match.
To re-filter a single timeline: `masstin -a merge -f case.csv --ignore-local -o case-filtered.csv`.
To keep only some dates, add `--start-time` and `--end-time`.

The masstin CSV: one row per connection or logon, sorted by time.
merge
The masstin action that joins several timelines into one.
verdict
The mark you put on a row (suspicious, benign...) in the `verdict` column.
--carry-marks
The option that copies verdicts and notes from an earlier timeline into the new one.
malformed row
A row with the wrong number of columns, nearly always because the CSV was saved from a spreadsheet.
.masstin file
A file that sits next to the timeline with what masstin knows about it.

learn: Unir varias timelines en una sola, ordenada y sin duplicados

steps: Reúne las timelines de cada entrega del caso.

Si has vuelto a analizar y tenías marcas, tráelas: `masstin -a merge -f nueva1.csv -f nueva2.csv -o caso-v2.csv --carry-marks caso-v1.csv`.
Mira cuántas filas recuperaron su marca y compáralo con las marcadas en la anterior: deben coincidir.
Para refiltrar una sola timeline: `masstin -a merge -f caso.csv --ignore-local -o caso-filtrado.csv`.
Para quedarte solo con unas fechas, añade `--start-time` y `--end-time`.

El CSV de masstin: una fila por conexión o inicio de sesión, ordenada por hora.
merge
Acción de masstin que junta varias timelines en una.
veredicto
Marca que pones a una fila (sospechosa, benigna...) en la columna `verdict`.
--carry-marks
Opción que copia veredictos y notas de una timeline anterior a la nueva.

Fila con un número de columnas incorrecto, casi siempre por haber guardado el CSV con una hoja de cálculo.

Fichero que acompaña a la timeline con lo que masstin sabe de ella.

learn: Install Neo4j and load a masstin timeline into it

need: A CSV timeline generated with masstin
Neo4j installed and running
masstin installed
steps: Install Neo4j for your platform and open `http://localhost:7474`.
Load the timeline with `masstin -a load-neo4j -f timeline.csv --database localhost:7687 --user neo4j`.
Run the query under 'Ver todo el movimiento lateral' to see the whole graph.
Apply the one under 'Filtrar por rango temporal' with the period in which you suspect the attack began.

A graph database, which stores nodes and the relationships between them.

The Neo4j query language.
Node and edge
The node is each machine; the edge is the connection between two machines.
Relationship type
The label of the edge; masstin puts the user account there, normalised.
Machine account
The computer's own account in the domain; its name ends in `$`.
Pivoting
Using an already compromised machine as a stepping stone to reach others.

Base de datos de grafos, que guarda nodos y las relaciones entre ellos.

Lenguaje de consultas de Neo4j.

El nodo es cada máquina; la arista es la conexión entre dos máquinas.

learn: Remove from the timeline the rows that are not lateral movement with `--ignore-local`

need: masstin installed
A masstin timeline already made, or the evidence to produce it
steps: Parse without filters first and keep that full timeline: it is your evidence.
Try the filter without writing anything: `masstin -a parse -d /evidence -o timeline.csv --ignore-local --dry-run`.
Read the `Filter summary`: how many rows stay, how many go, and for which reason.
Apply the filter on a copy: `masstin -a merge -f case.csv --ignore-local --exclude-users '*$' -o filtered.csv`.
Add `--exclude-users`, `--exclude-hosts` or `--exclude-ips` only for what you have checked is noise in that network.
If a pattern takes far more rows than you expected, fix it before going on.
Do not exclude the jump server or machine accounts without thinking: they can be part of the attack.

An attacker moving from one machine to another inside the network.

The address a machine uses to talk to itself (`127.0.0.1` or `::1`).

The computer's own account in the domain; its name ends in `$`.

An intermediate machine administrators go through to reach the rest of the network.

A way to write a range of addresses, for example `10.99.0.0/16`.

An attack in which an account's authentication is forwarded from another address.

Aplica el filtro sobre una copia: `masstin -a merge -f caso.csv --ignore-local --exclude-users '*$' -o filtrado.csv`.
Añade `--exclude-users`, `--exclude-hosts` o `--exclude-ips` solo para lo que hayas comprobado que es ruido en esa red.
Si un patrón se lleva muchas más filas de las que esperabas, corrígelo antes de seguir.
No excluyas el servidor de salto ni las cuentas de máquina sin pensarlo: pueden ser parte del ataque.

Paso de un atacante de una máquina a otra dentro de la red.
loopback
Dirección con la que una máquina se habla a sí misma (`127.0.0.1` o `::1`).

Cuenta del propio equipo en el dominio; su nombre acaba en `$`.

Máquina intermedia por la que los administradores entran al resto de la red.

Forma de escribir un rango de direcciones, por ejemplo `10.99.0.0/16`.

Ataque en el que se reenvía la autenticación de una cuenta desde otra dirección.

Use `--rules` for logs masstin does not know and `--carve` to recover deleted events

An evidence folder: EVTX files, triages, disk images or Linux or macOS logs
steps: Put all the evidence of the case in one folder.
Run `masstin -a parse -d /evidence/case -o timeline.csv`.
Read the `Found:` line and check that masstin sees what you expected.
When it ends, look at the per-source breakdown and look for machines that produced nothing.
If you have logs from a VPN, a firewall or a proxy, add them: `masstin -a parse -d /evidence/case -f fortigate-vpn.log --rules rules/vpn -o timeline.csv`.

The file format of Windows event logs.

A quick collection of the most useful artefacts of a machine, without copying the whole disk.

A full copy of a disk in a file (E01, VMDK, VHD/VHDX, dd).

An older snapshot of the volume that can still hold earlier logs.

Going through the image byte by byte looking for loose records of deleted or overwritten logs.

learn: Analizar cualquier evidencia con una sola orden, sin saber antes de qué tipo es
